# Turning cellEditing off at runtime does nothing, and on again adds a second plugin

## Context

Leaf of #18762. Found while probing @neo-fable's unowned defect-note of 13:22Z (`cellEditing` turned on at runtime on a mounted grid opens a session that never embodies). **I did not reproduce her sighting** — see *What this ticket is not* below. I did find a different, reproducible defect in the same method.

Measured at `dev@0e3fb712ff`, real Chromium, on `examples/grid/container` — a plain grid that ships with `cellEditing: false` — driven through `Neo.worker.App.setConfigs`.

## The Problem

`grid.Container#cellEditing` is a reactive config, so an app may turn cell editing on and off at runtime. Turning it **off** does nothing, and turning it back **on** adds a second plugin.

| step | `cellEditing` | plugin `…-1` | plugin `…-2` |
|---|---|---|---|
| boot | `false` | absent | absent |
| set `true` | `true` | registered, `disabled: false` | absent |
| set `false` | **`false`** | **still registered, still `disabled: false`** | absent |
| set `true` again | `true` | registered, `disabled: false` | **registered, `disabled: false`** |

Two consequences, one cause:

1. **`cellEditing: false` is a no-op.** The config reads `false` while the plugin remains registered and enabled. An app that switches editing off has not switched it off.
2. **Every off→on cycle pushes another plugin instance.** N cycles leave N+1 live plugins on one grid, each with its own `session` field.

The second bears directly on this epic's terminal predicate. #18762 states *"One editor instance per session; commit or cancel destroys it"*, and the guide states *"One editor exists at a time. Activating another cell commits the current draft first."* Two plugin instances each own an independent `session`, so the invariant is held by each plugin separately and by neither of them jointly.

## The Architectural Reality

`src/grid/Container.mjs:374-392`:

```javascript
afterSetCellEditing(value, oldValue) {
    if (value) {
        import('./plugin/CellEditing.mjs').then(module => {
            let me        = this,
                {appName} = me,
                plugins   = me.plugins || [];

            plugins.push({module: module.default, appName});

            me.plugins = plugins;

            // The plugin arrives after an import, so rows may have rendered without it
            me.repaintCells()
        })
    }
}
```

The whole body is one `if (value)`. There is no `else`, so nothing tears the plugin down; and there is no check for an already-present plugin, so the `push` is unconditional. `oldValue` is declared in the signature and never read — the parameter that would distinguish "first enable" from "re-enable" is right there, unused.

The plugin itself already has the vocabulary for both halves: `disabled_` with an `afterSetDisabled` that cancels an open edit (`src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs:47-71`), and a `'destroy'` cancel reason documented at `:82` for "the plugin went, its grid lives on". So the teardown semantics this method needs are defined and unused from here.

## The Fix

Make `afterSetCellEditing` idempotent and give it its off branch, in `src/grid/Container.mjs`:

- **On `true`:** if a `grid-cell-editing` plugin is already present, do not push another — re-enable the existing one.
- **On `false`:** stop editing. The plugin's own `disabled` config already cancels an open edit and refuses new ones, so the minimal correct behaviour is reachable without teardown; destroying the plugin is the alternative and is what the `'destroy'` cancel reason anticipates. The implementer picks one and states it in the AC.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `grid.Container#cellEditing_` (public reactive config, `Container.mjs:118-121`) | its own JSDoc + #18762's one-editor predicate | reactive both ways; idempotent on repeat | today: `false` is inert, repeats accumulate plugins | `learn/guides/datahandling/Grids.md` "Turning It On" documents only construction-time use | the table above |
| `grid.plugin.CellEditing#disabled_` (`CellEditing.mjs:47-50`) | `afterSetDisabled` → `cancelEdit('disabled')` at `:65-71` | the off branch's mechanism, if teardown is not chosen | n/a | — | measured today: setting it cancels an open edit, discards the draft, returns focus to the View |

## Decision Record impact

`none` — restores the declared behaviour of one reactive config.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1** After `cellEditing` is set to `false` at runtime, a double-click on a previously editable cell starts no edit. Red on `dev` today.
- **AC-2** Setting `cellEditing` `true` → `false` → `true` leaves exactly **one** `plugin-grid-cell-editing` instance on the grid. Red on `dev` today (two instances).
- **AC-3** Setting `cellEditing: true` twice in a row, with no intervening `false`, also leaves exactly one instance.
- **AC-4** ~~After the off→on cycle, a double-click opens exactly **one** editor.~~ **— moved to #18966.**
- **AC-5** ~~An edit open when `cellEditing` goes `false` is cancelled, not committed.~~ **— moved to #18966.**
- **AC-6** Mutation-proven: reverting the idempotence guard reddens AC-2/AC-3; reverting the off branch reddens AC-1.

**AC-4 and AC-5 moved, and why** (2026-09-19, by this ticket's author, before the PR opened): both describe a live edit session, which the single-thread unit harness cannot mount — creating one drives `form.field.Text` into `registerPreventDefaultKeys`, a `Neo.main.DomEvents` call with no main thread behind it. Measured: the arm's assertions passed and teardown then threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'registerPreventDefaultKeys')`. They belong on the `grid-cell-editing` component fixture and now live in #18966, on the #18863 → #18927 pattern. AC-1 stayed here because the refusal is assertable without a session: `startEdit` returns `false` while the plugin is disabled.

## Out of Scope

@neo-fable's runtime-enable sighting (below) — it may or may not share this cause, and I will not claim it does. The lazy-import timing itself, which the existing `repaintCells()` comment already addresses. Any change to `plugin.Base`'s lifecycle generally.

## What this ticket is NOT — the honest bound

@neo-fable's note describes a **first** runtime enable on `apps/workstation`'s feed grid where the session opens but never embodies. **I did not reproduce that**, and this ticket is not it. Two live plugins is a plausible mechanism for a session that one instance opens and another never renders, but her sighting has no toggle in it, so the mechanisms are not the same until someone shows they are.

What blocked the faithful repro, so the next seat does not rediscover it: `examples/grid/container`'s columns carry no `editable`, and with the Neural Link bridge down (`BRIDGE_EXIT_1`, `neo-agent-brain#371`) there is no main-thread path to set a column config — `Neo.worker.App.getConfigs` reads configs but cannot reach column instances by id, and asking the grid for `plugins` or `columns` hangs the call. A seat with a working Neural Link, or an example with `editable` columns and `cellEditing: false` at construction, closes that gap cheaply.

## Avoided Traps

- **Do not read AC-2 as the whole defect.** An instance count is easy to satisfy and easy to regress without anyone noticing; AC-4 is what a user would feel.
- **Do not assume `disabled: true` on the plugin equals `cellEditing: false` on the container.** They are different surfaces today, and the ticket's point is that the container's one is inert.
- **Do not fold @neo-fable's sighting in to make this ticket bigger.** One measured cause, one ticket.
